newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia-China wool trade safe despite rejection.
newsitem.headline: Australia-China wool trade safe despite rejection.

text.p: The rejection by China of a wool shipment from Australia was related to certification and would not disturb the trade, a spokesman for Australian Minister for Primary Industries John Anderson told Reuters.
An Australian government official in Beijing was negotiating over certification, Anderson's spokesman said.
"It is not a great problem," he said.
"The wool trade is continuing to China as normal, they are in the market this week heavily buying," he said.
It was thought that the case may not be over anthrax, despite reports that anthrax was involved in the certification problem, he said. The matter is under investigation.
"There's no affect on trade," he said.
The case involves a shipment of Australian wool tops at the southern Chinese port of Xiamen.
Anderson's spokesman pointed out that China had accepted greasy wool imports from Australia regardless of the anthrax outbreak months ago.
It was most unlikely that heat-treated wool tops would contain anthrax, he said.
